title: ILO and Bangladesh Labour Foundation start child labour project in Keraniganj garment hub
excerpt: The one-year project targets 4,500 children in two unions. BLF estimates 120,000 children work in Keraniganj's informal garment units.
content:
The International Labour Organization (ILO) and Bangladesh Labour Foundation (BLF) on Tuesday (24 November) launched a project to reduce child labour in the informal garment sector of Keraniganj, south of Dhaka, The Daily Star reported.

The project runs from October 2026 to September 2027 in Aganagar and Suvadda unions. It targets 4,500 children, including 900 under 14. It aims to stop children being recruited, take them out of hazardous work, return younger children to school, and offer safer work and skills training to adolescents.

According to BLF, Keraniganj's garment hub has about 7,500 production units employing more than 250,000 workers. It estimates that 120,000 children work there, about 20,000 of them under 14. BLF executive director A K M Ashraf Uddin said he had met children aged 10, 11 and 12 who had never been to school but were already working.

Speaking at the launch, Prime Minister's Adviser Dr Mahdi Amin said the government is preparing a National Plan of Action on child labour for 2026-30. He said plans include more mid-day meals, uniforms and stipends, free education gradually extended to Class VIII, more technical education, and raising education spending to 5% of GDP.

Other speakers called for more labour inspections and compulsory education to age 14. ILO representatives said child labour cannot end without tackling families' financial hardship. Michal Krejza of the EU Delegation warned of the consequences for trade and investment.

Why it matters

Keraniganj supplies the domestic clothing market and sits outside the export sector's buyer audits, so child labour there is largely unchecked. The project reaches only a small share of the estimated 120,000 children. What the national action plan funds will decide whether the approach can grow.

What to watch

Publication of the 2026-30 National Plan of Action, and whether stipends and school meals are budgeted for areas with high child labour.

Sources
